Sam — thanks for the clarifications. Below is a concise sketch of pricing and the latency vs cost trade-offs tailored to your numbers. I'll bring Dev into the call to validate technical knobs.

Unit economics (illustrative) — total tokens = input + output
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): $10 / 1M tokens (standard tier, streaming supported).
  - Pros: zero setup, flexible scale, immediate onboarding.
  - Cons: higher per-token price at scale; p99 guarantees are best-effort (we publish p50/p95/p99 profiles but not SLA-backed at this tier).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): $6 / 1M tokens (with a committed monthly spend).
  - Pros: predictable unit cost, reserved GPU pools -> better p99 latency.
  - Cons: commit required; provisioning lead time for large pools.
- Dedicated w/ SLA uplift: $8 / 1M tokens (includes priority routing + SLA-backed p99 target).

Monthly cost examples for your band (12-15M tokens/month):
- Hosted at $10/1M => $120 - $150 per month.
- Dedicated at $6/1M => $72 - $90 per month.
- Dedicated w/ SLA uplift at $8/1M => $96 - $120 per month.

Note: these $ amounts are illustrative and assume "tokens" are counted as input+output. At the token volumes you quoted, the per-month dollar amounts above are modest relative to the budget bands you shared. If your finance team expects $8k-12k/month for the pilot, that implies either a different token baseline (e.g., tens or hundreds of billions of tokens) or additional managed services and support/hosting fees. Please confirm the token accounting you're using so we can align the forecast.

Latency vs cost trade-offs (how to reason about SLOs):
- Batching: larger batch sizes reduce per-token compute overhead and lower unit cost but increase tail latency. For interactive flows (p95 < 300ms) we recommend small batch windows (sub-100ms or adaptive micro-batching) plus streaming to reduce perceived latency.
- Streaming: improves perceived latency for long responses; does not materially change total compute cost. Supported in Hosted and Dedicated.
- Reserved capacity (Dedicated): buying GPU pools and capacity headroom improves p99 because we can isolate noisy neighbors and pin optimized model variants/quantization. If you need p99 <= 800ms consistently at peak concurrency (30-50 QPS), Dedicated or SLA-backed Dedicated is the safer path.
- SLO-driven pricing: we offer a commercial uplift for SLA-backed p99 targets to cover reserved capacity and priority routing (example band shown above).

Recommended next steps:
1) Confirm the "tokens" metric (input+output vs. generated-only) so I can produce a per-month cost mapping that matches your finance assumptions.
2) Technical slot: Wed 21 May, 10am PT — 30-45m with Dev to validate batch & cache settings and run a quick cost projection for a dedicated canary.
3) Quick proof option: start Hosted with streaming + prefix caching; monitor cost and tails for 2 weeks; if p99 or cost are off, migrate to a small Dedicated pool for a canary.
